subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Hepatocellular carcinoma: screening, staging and multidisciplinary systemic management

steps.tx: The **Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer** (BCLC) staging schema integrates tumour burden, baseline liver reserve evaluated by **Child-Pugh** classification, and performance status. Spanning from stage 0 very early disease to stage D terminal liver failure, BCLC directly links prognosis to evidence-based treatment interventions. Preserving underlying background hepatic function remains as critical as treating the tumour itself during every treatment decision.

steps.tx: Non-invasive radiological diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma follows strict **LI-RADS** computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging criteria. In cirrhotic patients, hallmark diagnostic criteria include intense **arterial phase hyperenhancement** followed by delayed venous phase washout and an enhancing capsule. When classical imaging hallmarks are present on multiphasic contrast examinations, histological tissue confirmation by invasive biopsy is unnecessary.
steps.say: Non-invasive radiological diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma follows strict LI-RADS computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging criteria. steps.tx: The paired liver scans show **arterial phase hyperenhancement** of a right lobe mass followed by delayed **washout** with an enhancing capsule. In a cirrhotic liver this classic sequence meets **LI RADS** criteria for definitive cancer. Recognizing the pattern matters because confident imaging diagnosis can establish hepatocellular carcinoma without invasive biopsy.
steps.say: These axial liver scans compare late arterial and delayed phases of a right lobe mass. The lesion enhances brightly in the arterial phase then washes out with a visible capsule later. In cirrhosis this classic behavior defines hepatocellular carcinoma by imaging criteria, so tissue biopsy is unnecessary and management can proceed directly.

steps.tx: First-line systemic therapy for **unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma** was revolutionized by the phase 3 **IMbrave150** trial. Combining the programmed death-ligand 1 inhibitor **atezolizumab** with the vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitor **bevacizumab** significantly prolonged overall survival and progression-free survival compared to **sorafenib**. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy to evaluate and manage esophageal varices is mandatory prior to initiating bevacizumab to avert fatal variceal hemorrhage.
steps.say: First-line systemic therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma was revolutionized by the phase 3 IMbrave150 trial. Combining the programmed death-ligand 1 inhibitor atezolizumab with the vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitor bevacizumab significantly prolonged overall survival compared to sorafenib. Endoscopy to manage esophageal varices is mandatory prior to treatment.

right.title: Sorafenib Monotherapy
points: Frequent hand-foot skin reactions and fatigue

steps.tx: Dual immune checkpoint inhibition provides an additional front-line therapeutic milestone in the **HIMALAYA trial**. The **STRIDE regimen** incorporates a single priming dose of the CTLA-4 inhibitor **tremelimumab** followed by regular interval **durvalumab** every 4 weeks. This innovative combination demonstrated statistically significant overall survival superiority over **sorafenib**, offering a valuable alternative for patients with contraindications to VEGF-targeted agents.

steps.tx: Oral multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain key components of the therapeutic armamentarium. In the **REFLECT trial**, **lenvatinib** proved non-inferior in overall survival to **sorafenib** while yielding significantly higher **objective response rate** and progression-free survival. Lenvatinib inhibits VEGFR 1 through 3, FGFR 1 through 4, RET, and KIT, making it particularly effective in patients displaying high tumour burden or portal vein branch thrombosis.

steps.tx: Transarterial **chemoembolization** (TACE) represents the benchmark locoregional therapy for intermediate stage **BCLC-B** disease. In patients with preserved liver function and absent macrovascular invasion, selective embolization of tumour feeding arterioles with cytotoxic emulsions induces profound ischemic necrosis. Careful patient selection prevents post-embolization liver failure, and sequential transition to systemic therapy is warranted upon TACE refractoriness.

In patients with preserved liver function and absent macrovascular invasion, selective embolization of tumour feeding arterioles induces profound ischemic necrosis. steps.tx: The left angiogram shows a **microcatheter** in the hepatic artery feeding nodular tumours labelled BCLC-B disease, with contrast holding in tumour vessels during **chemoembolization**. The right panel shows a widely opacified liver with preserved background parenchyma and no macrovascular invasion. The pairing matters because selective delivery of embolic particles plus cytotoxic emulsion causes tumour **ischemia** while sparing liver reserve, which guides choice and timing of locoregional therapy.
steps.say: The left frame shows a fine catheter placed into the liver artery supplying lower tumours, with dark retained contrast marking treated tumour vessels. The right frame shows the whole liver still filling well, with open portal branches and healthy background tissue. In intermediate stage disease with good liver reserve and no large vessel invasion, this selective blockade starves tumours while protecting function. The image links catheter position, tumour filling, and preserved liver to the decision for locoregional treatment.

vis.alt: The paired angiograms show a microcatheter delivering embolic material to lower liver tumours beside a preserved liver without large vessel invasion.
vis.caption: Paired hepatic angiograms show selective tumour embolization with preserved liver, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Orthotopic **liver transplantation** offers the unique advantage of eliminating both the malignancy and underlying cirrhotic parenchymal disease. The **Milan criteria** establish eligibility for deceased-donor transplantation: a single nodule 5 cm or smaller, or up to 3 nodules each 3 cm or smaller, without macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic spread. Meeting these criteria achieves excellent post-transplant five-year survival exceeding seventy percent.

steps.tx: Serum **alpha-fetoprotein** serves as a vital prognostic biomarker and surveillance tool in liver oncology. In a known **cirrhotic patient** presenting with a new hypervascular liver nodule, an AFP concentration of 400 ng/mL or higher provides strong diagnostic confirmation of hepatocellular carcinoma. Post-treatment serial measurements of alpha-fetoprotein detect early disease recurrence prior to obvious radiological tumour progression.

points: Can occur in early small HCC lesions
Seen in chronic hepatitis or cirrhosis flares
Relies strictly on multiphasic MRI imaging
